bars.label: New tests that failed on main and pass now

body:
**You were right: trunk push was already on before the install.** Harmonize's CLAUDE.md gives the permission (2026-11-09), and the installer wrote it off anyway because it never read that file.

## What changes

- **First install:** trunk push turns on when the repo's own `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` (or `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`) already says pushing `main` is allowed. The installer prints where it found it, e.g. `trunk push: on (the repo already grants it: CLAUDE.md:3: ...)`. The permission mode comes from `.claude/settings.json` (or `settings.local.json`) `defaultMode` when that is a permissive mode (auto, acceptEdits, bypassPermissions, dontAsk).
- **The terminal wizard (`--tui`):** it now starts from the same answer. When the repo grants trunk push, the wizard's default is yes and the summary shows `Push main: yes (granted in CLAUDE.md:3)`. Changing the autonomy level no longer flips it back to no, and a run with no screen (headless) keeps it too. You can still pick no on the screen. The installer and the wizard share one reader (`scripts/step0_scan.py`), so they cannot disagree.
- **Nothing grants it:** run in a terminal, the installer asks once. Run by an agent, it stays off and prints `ask the owner once, then rerun with --trunk-push yes`. A stranger's repo still starts off. A line that says no ("Never push main", "do not push to main") is not read as a yes.
- **Rerun or `--update`:** it never turns off anything already on in `.kit/config.json`. That covers trunk push, the four autonomy switches and any other on/off setting you set; the permission mode stays as it is. Each one it holds back prints `KEPT kit.<key>: on`. The only way to turn one off is to edit that file. An update does not read CLAUDE.md again, so a choice you made later still wins.
- **README:** the install section says this in two lines, ahead of the "ask the owner once" question.

## Tests (`tests/test_install_permissions.py`, 11)

These fail on main and pass with the change: Harmonize's real line turns it on, an AGENTS.md line turns it on, `defaultMode` sets the permission mode, a repo with none stays off, `--update --trunk-push no` keeps it on, `--autonomy gated` on a rerun keeps the autonomy switches on, the wizard defaults to yes with Harmonize's line (for each autonomy level and headless).
These already passed on main and still do: `--trunk-push yes`, `--update` keeps the permission mode and any on/off setting of yours, `--update` does not read CLAUDE.md over your choice, the wizard stays at no in a repo that grants nothing.

I merged origin/main again (CL11's board token arrived), then ran `python3 scripts/run_all_tests.py`: **8/8 suites, 0 failed**. Nothing on WHAT-NOT-TO-BREAK was touched: the KEPT logic for files is unchanged and permissions get the same treatment.
not_checked: Not run on Harmonize itself: its config is already true (set by hand), so this change only keeps it that way.
The wizard's clickable screen was not driven by hand. Tests cover its defaults, its headless run and its summary; the tap path calls the same function.
The kit repo's own .kit/config.json in git still says trunk_push false. I left it alone, as the orchestrator holds that setting.
title: The install keeps permissions you already gave
verdict: The install and the terminal wizard no longer turn off a permission you gave. Branch cl22-install-keeps-permissions (88ef283) includes the latest main, and all 8 test suites pass. Ready for the orchestrator to merge.
